segmentReportingChange.effectiveQuarter: FY2027 Q1 (quarter ended 26 April 2026; first reported 20 May 2026)
segmentReportingChange.description: Beginning with the first quarter of fiscal 2027 NVIDIA reports two market platforms -- Data Center and Edge Computing -- replacing the previous five markets (Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, Automotive, OEM & Other). Within Data Center, NVIDIA reports two sub-markets: (1) Hyperscale, which includes revenue from the public clouds and the world's largest consumer internet companies; and (2) ACIE, which incorporates AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise, and addresses NVIDIA's growth opportunity in diverse AI purpose-built data centers and AI factories across industries and countries. Edge Computing highlights data processing devices for agentic and physical AI including PCs, game consoles, workstations, AI-RAN base stations, robotics and automotive. Gaming is no longer broken out separately. The previous Data Center Compute / Networking sub-market table is also discontinued, though NVIDIA disclosed those figures in narrative form for Q1 FY2027 only ('Under the previous sub-markets, Data Center compute revenue was a record $60.4 billion... Data Center networking revenue was a record $14.8 billion'). The two REPORTABLE SEGMENTS under ASC 280 -- Compute & Networking and Graphics -- are unchanged.
segmentReportingChange.rationale: NVIDIA's stated rationale, verbatim from the Q1 FY2027 CFO Commentary: 'Following the rapid evolution in our businesses, we are transitioning to a new reporting framework that better reflects our current and future growth drivers.' The Q1 FY2027 press release states: 'NVIDIA is transitioning to a new reporting framework that better reflects its current and future growth drivers.'

restatedPriorPeriods.note: NVIDIA restated only two prior quarters onto the new basis, in the Q1 FY2027 comparative columns. No restatement was published for any quarter before FY2026 Q1.

segmentReportingChange.bridgeFromOldToNew: Verified against the restated comparatives: the new Data Center total is IDENTICAL to the old Data Center market (FY2026 Q1 $39,112M; FY2026 Q4 $62,314M), and new Edge Computing equals the exact arithmetic sum of the four former non-Data-Center markets (FY2026 Q1: Gaming 3,763 + ProViz 509 + Automotive 567 + OEM & Other 111 = 4,950 = Edge Computing; FY2026 Q4: 3,727 + 1,321 + 604 + 161 = 5,813 = Edge Computing). Hyperscale + ACIE sums exactly to Data Center. This bridge is stated as an observed reconciliation of NVIDIA-disclosed figures, not as an estimate.

stockSplits.detail: Executed 19 July 2021. Stockholders of record at the close of business on 21 June 2021 received a dividend of three additional shares for every share held.

Announced May 2024 and effected by amendment to the Restated Certificate of Incorporation filed June 2024. Shareholders of record at the close of market on 6 June 2024 received nine additional shares, distributed after the close of market on 7 June 2024. Authorized common stock increased from 8.0 billion to 80.0 billion shares.

caveats: Convention: every figure is AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED in that quarter's own earnings 8-K (press release + CFO Commentary), so each quarter row is internally consistent with the segment data disclosed alongside it. Where NVIDIA later restated a figure, the restated value is given in that quarter's 'notes' and in 'verification'.
EPS is pre-split throughout. NVIDIA executed a 4-for-1 split in July 2021 and a 10-for-1 split in June 2024; multiply by 1/40 to compare with today's share count.

FY2017 Q1 and Q2 net income and diluted EPS were restated upward (+$12M / +$8M) when NVIDIA early-adopted ASU 2016-09 in Q3 FY2017 retroactive to 1 Feb 2016. As-reported quarters sum to FY2017 net income of $1,646M; the audited FY2017 figure is $1,666M.

Market-platform revenue was not published for FY2016 quarters at the time; NVIDIA only disclosed the older GPU / Tegra Processor / Other operating-segment split. The FY2016 market-platform values here are NVIDIA's own subsequent disclosure, read from the prior-year comparison columns of the FY2017 CFO Commentaries.

Segment labels changed over time: 'Datacenter' -> 'Data Center' and 'OEM and IP' -> 'OEM and Other', both effective with the Q1 FY2020 CFO Commentary. The series is continuous; only the label changed. Mapped to dataCenter and oemAndOther here.

Quarterly figures are each rounded to $1M by NVIDIA, so summing four quarters can differ from the audited annual figure by $1-2M on gross profit, operating expenses, operating income, R&D and net income. Quarterly revenue sums to the annual figure exactly in all six fiscal years.
FY2021 (calendar Feb 2020 - Jan 2021) includes Mellanox from 27 Apr 2020, which is the main driver of the Q2 FY2021 step-up in Data Center revenue and operating expenses.

Fiscal Q4 is never tagged as a standalone period in SEC XBRL (the 10-K tags the full year), so Q4 figures were verified against the audited annual totals disclosed in the same Q4 press release rather than against a standalone XBRL frame.
grossMarginPct is NVIDIA's stated GAAP gross margin from the CFO Commentary. It agrees with grossProfit/revenue from the press-release income statement to within 0.05pp for all 24 quarters.
All figures are GAAP. Non-GAAP figures published alongside them were deliberately not used.

SEGMENT REPORTING CHANGE, FY2027 Q1: see meta.segmentReportingChange for the full description, NVIDIA's verbatim rationale, the effective quarter, source URLs, and the old-to-new bridge. For FY2027 Q1 the fields gaming, proVisualization, automotive and oemAndOther are null because NVIDIA no longer discloses them; conversely dataCenterHyperscale, dataCenterAcie and edgeComputing are null for all quarters before FY2027 Q1 as originally reported (restated FY2026 Q1 and FY2026 Q4 values are held in meta.segmentReportingChange.restatedPriorPeriods rather than in the quarter objects, to keep every quarter object on an as-originally-reported basis).

Q4 QUARTERS ARE NOT XBRL-TAGGED. NVIDIA files a Form 10-K rather than a Q4 Form 10-Q, so no ~91-day XBRL duration exists for any fourth quarter. Q4 income-statement and segment values therefore come from the Q4 earnings press release and CFO Commentary (Form 8-K Exhibits 99.1/99.2). They were independently reconciled by subtracting the Q3 Form 10-Q nine-month year-to-date figures from the Form 10-K fiscal-year figures; all such checks matched exactly (see the verification array). FY2022 Q4 could not be reconciled this way because the FY2022 Q1-Q3 Forms 10-Q predate NVIDIA's revenue-by-market disaggregation note, so FY2022 was instead validated by confirming that the four quarterly figures sum exactly to the FY2022 Form 10-K fiscal-year revenue by market.

DILUTED EPS IS ON THREE DIFFERENT SHARE BASES across this series because it is recorded as originally reported. See meta.epsPolicy and meta.stockSplits. Do not chart dilutedEps as a continuous series without adjusting.

DATA CENTER COMPUTE / NETWORKING SUB-MARKET SPLIT is only available for FY2025 Q1 through FY2026 Q4. NVIDIA began tabulating it in Q1 FY2025 and discontinued the table in Q1 FY2027. For FY2027 Q1 the two figures are disclosed in narrative form only and rounded by NVIDIA to $0.1 billion ($60.4B compute, $14.8B networking); they are recorded here as 60400 and 14800 and are NOT precise to $1 million. All quarters from FY2022 Q1 to FY2024 Q4 are null.

SUPPLY COMMITMENTS ARE NOT A CONSISTENT TIME SERIES. NVIDIA changed both the wording and the scope of this disclosure several times; supplyCommitmentsLabel records NVIDIA's exact term for each quarter. Three distinct bases appear: (a) FY2022 Q1 through FY2026 Q1 -- inventory purchase and long-term supply (and, from FY2024 Q1, capacity) obligations, i.e. manufacturing/supply only; (b) FY2026 Q2 -- 'Total future commitments' of $45,774M on a materially BROADER basis that also includes software and technology licences, investments, long-lived assets and multi-year cloud service agreements, and is therefore NOT comparable with the quarters either side of it; (c) FY2026 Q3 onward -- manufacturing, supply and capacity commitments, with multi-year cloud service agreement commitments disclosed SEPARATELY ($26.0B at FY2026 Q3, $27.0B at FY2026 Q4, $30.0B at FY2027 Q1) and excluded from the figure recorded here.

QUARTERLY OPERATING CASH FLOW FOR Q2, Q3 AND Q4 IS NOT AVAILABLE FROM XBRL. NVIDIA's Forms 10-Q present the cash flow statement on a year-to-date basis, so only Q1 has a ~91-day XBRL duration. Quarterly operatingCashFlow and freeCashFlow are therefore taken from the three-month column of the free-cash-flow reconciliation table in each earnings press release. This column selection was validated by confirming that all six Q1 values match the XBRL three-month figures exactly, and that the four quarters of FY2022 sum exactly to the reported fiscal-year figure of $9,108M. Note that in some years the four as-reported quarterly figures differ from the reported fiscal-year total by $1-2M due to independent rounding (e.g. FY2023 quarters sum to $5,643M vs $5,641M reported for the year); the as-reported quarterly values are retained unchanged.

FREE CASH FLOW IS A NON-GAAP MEASURE, defined by NVIDIA as GAAP net cash provided by operating activities less both purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets and principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets. Every other figure in this dataset is GAAP.

NON-GAAP DEFINITION CHANGE, FY2027 Q1: beginning in Q1 FY2027 NVIDIA's non-GAAP measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense, and its historical non-GAAP information was updated accordingly. This does not affect any figure in this dataset (all are GAAP) but it does mean externally published non-GAAP NVIDIA history changed basis at the same time as the segment reporting change.

FY2026 Q1 CONTAINS A $4.5 BILLION CHARGE for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations following the April 2025 US export licence requirement, which depressed GAAP gross margin to 60.5% from the mid-70s trend. $4.6B of H20 sales were recognised in the quarter before the restriction and a further $2.5B could not be shipped. FY2027 Q1 had no Data Center Hopper shipments to China.
FY2023 Q1 OPERATING EXPENSES OF $3,563M INCLUDE A $1,353M ARM ACQUISITION TERMINATION COST, which is why operating expenses jump and operating income falls versus adjacent quarters.

Values are recorded exactly as disclosed. Nothing in this dataset is interpolated, estimated or reconstructed; every field that could not be sourced is null and is listed in the unavailable array.
